Buyer & owner journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it.

01

Discover and enquire

Buyers compare models, variants, on-road prices and waiting periods across OEM sites, marketplaces and social media, then enquire by form, call or WhatsApp, often after work hours. Pre-owned buyers browse listings, and sellers ask what their vehicle is worth.

Touchpoints

  • OEM website and lead portal
  • Marketplace listings and dealer panels
  • Meta and Google lead forms
  • Click-to-WhatsApp and missed-call numbers
  • Walk-ins and showroom calls

Accountable owner

CRM or digital lead manager

Automations on this stage

Discover and enquire · 3–5 weeks

Instant lead response, qualification and routing

Leads from OEM portals, the website, ad lead forms, marketplaces, missed calls and WhatsApp are deduplicated, acknowledged within minutes where the buyer has opted in, qualified with a short flow and assigned to a consultant with a first-call timer.

View the blueprint ↗Discover and enquire · 4–6 weeks

Inspection-led listings synced to the website and marketplaces

Once a vehicle passes inspection and refurbishment, listing text is drafted from the structured inspection report, approved by the used-car manager and published to the website and marketplace dealer panels from one record. Reserved and sold vehicles come down everywhere.

View the blueprint ↗
02

Test drive and evaluation

The buyer drives the shortlisted model at the showroom or at home, and owners who want to sell or exchange a vehicle book an inspection. Consultants and evaluators need the right demo vehicle or inspection slot in the right place.

Touchpoints

  • Showroom and home test drives
  • Demo fleet calendar
  • Exchange and trade-in evaluation
  • Doorstep or yard inspection

Accountable owner

Sales team leader and evaluation manager

Automations on this stage

Test drive and evaluation · 3–4 weeks

Test-drive and test-ride booking against the demo fleet

Buyers pick showroom or home test drives from slots tied to real demo-vehicle availability by variant and branch, get reminders and can reschedule in one tap. Consultants see the day's schedule and get a follow-up prompt after each drive.

View the blueprint ↗Test drive and evaluation · 3–5 weeks

Seller and exchange evaluation booking

Owners who want to sell or exchange share vehicle details and photos in a short WhatsApp flow, book a yard or doorstep inspection and receive an offer only after an evaluator has inspected the vehicle and a manager has approved the price.

View the blueprint ↗
03

Quote, finance and booking

The consultant prepares an on-road price, exchange value and offers, the finance and insurance desk takes over loan and cover options, and the buyer pays a booking amount.

Touchpoints

  • On-road price quote
  • Exchange offer
  • Finance desk and lender referral
  • Insurance quote
  • Booking receipt

Accountable owner

Sales manager and finance and insurance desk head

Automations on this stage

Quote, finance and booking · 5–7 weeks

On-road quote with finance and insurance desk handoff

Consultants issue consistent on-road quotes from approved price lists and insurer quotes, with optional items shown as clear opt-ins. Finance and insurance requests move to the F&I desk with the buyer's consent, and lender disclosures and decisions stay with the lender.

View the blueprint ↗
04

Allotment, paperwork and delivery

The vehicle is allotted, payments and loan disbursal complete, insurance is issued, registration or ownership transfer is filed, plates are fitted and the vehicle is handed over. Each item has its own owner and its own delays.

Touchpoints

  • Allotment and waiting-period updates
  • Loan disbursal and payment
  • Vahan registration or transfer
  • HSRP fitment
  • Pre-delivery inspection and handover
  • PM E-DRIVE e-voucher for eligible EVs

Accountable owner

Delivery coordinator and registration executive

Automations on this stage

Allotment, paperwork and delivery · 4–6 weeks

Booking-to-delivery tracker with waiting-period updates

Every booking gets one tracker for allotment, payments, loan disbursal, insurance, registration, accessories and pre-delivery inspection. Buyers get regular status updates in approved wording, and coordinators see what is blocking each delivery.

View the blueprint ↗Allotment, paperwork and delivery · 2–4 weeks

Registration, HSRP and RC status tracking

After invoicing, each vehicle's registration checklist, Vahan application, tax payment, number plate fitment and RC dispatch are tracked with a named owner. Buyers get status updates, and registration staff see what is missing before the file is submitted.

View the blueprint ↗Allotment, paperwork and delivery · 4–5 weeks

Ownership transfer and RC document tracker for used vehicles

Every vehicle bought or sold gets a transfer file covering Form 29C intimation, Forms 29 and 30, hypothecation removal and NOCs, with reminders to whoever owes the next document and alerts before statutory reporting windows close.

View the blueprint ↗Allotment, paperwork and delivery · 3–5 weeks

EV subsidy document checks and ownership onboarding

For eligible EV sales, the model is checked against the current PM E-DRIVE list, buyer details are checked before the e-voucher is generated, and signed e-voucher status is tracked. New owners then get approved onboarding messages on charging, range, app pairing and first service.

View the blueprint ↗
05

Service and repair

Owners return for periodic, running and warranty repairs. They book, hand over the vehicle or ask for pick-up, approve additional work and collect the vehicle with an invoice they understand.

Touchpoints

  • Service due reminders
  • Online and WhatsApp booking
  • Pick-up and drop
  • Job card and estimate approval
  • Ready-for-delivery and invoice

Accountable owner

Works manager and service advisors

Automations on this stage

Service and repair · 2–4 weeks

Service, PUC and battery check reminders by date and distance

Due dates are calculated per vehicle from the OEM schedule, the last service and average daily kilometers from job-card odometer readings. Consenting owners get reminders with one-tap booking, and owners who stop coming go to a call list.

View the blueprint ↗Service and repair · 4–5 weeks

Online service booking with pick-up and drop

Owners book on WhatsApp or the website against advisor and bay capacity, describe concerns in their own words and request pick-up. Drivers get assigned runs and record timestamped condition photos, and owners can follow the vehicle until it is back.

View the blueprint ↗Service and repair · 4–6 weeks

Job-card status and customer approval for additional work

When technicians find additional work, the advisor sends an itemized estimate with photos or video, and the owner approves or declines each line. Work starts only after approval is recorded, and the owner gets status updates until the vehicle is ready.

View the blueprint ↗
06

Feedback, renewals and upgrade

After delivery and each service the owner rates the experience, renews insurance, considers an extended warranty and, in time, exchanges the vehicle. Unhappy owners need a call, not another survey.

Touchpoints

  • Post-delivery and post-service feedback
  • Complaint call-back
  • Insurance renewal
  • Extended warranty offers
  • Exchange and upgrade enquiries

Accountable owner

Customer relations manager

Automations on this stage

Feedback, renewals and upgrade · 3–4 weeks

Post-delivery and post-service feedback with service recovery

A short feedback request follows each delivery and service visit. Low ratings, repeat concerns and complaints become tickets with the job or sale history attached, and a named person calls the owner back within the agreed time.

View the blueprint ↗Feedback, renewals and upgrade · 3–4 weeks

Consented insurance renewal and extended-warranty reminders

Owners who agreed to renewal messages get reminders before policy and warranty expiry. Insurance renewals go to the designated insurance executive for owners the dealership may serve under its insurer appointment, and extended warranties are offered only while the vehicle is eligible.

Where people stay in control

Human checkpoints across the journey.

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Instant lead response, qualification and routingDiscover and enquireThe sales consultant makes the first call and answers anything about price, discounts, exchange value or finance. Team leaders handle reassignment, and the sales manager approves templates, qualifying questions and routing rules before launch and after every change.
Inspection-led listings synced to the website and marketplacesDiscover and enquireThe used-car manager approves price, condition notes and disclosures such as accident, flood or repaint history before anything is published. Pricing suggestions are never applied automatically.
Test-drive and test-ride booking against the demo fleetTest drive and evaluationThe consultant confirms every home test drive, checks the driving license before handing over keys and decides whether the drive goes ahead. The showroom manager sets the home-drive radius, time limits and which variants may leave the showroom.
Seller and exchange evaluation bookingTest drive and evaluationThe evaluator inspects every vehicle in person, and the used-car manager approves each offer price. No automated price is ever quoted to a seller.
On-road quote with finance and insurance desk handoffQuote, finance and bookingThe sales manager approves discounts and exchange values above limits. The lender makes every credit decision and issues its Key Facts Statement; the dealership shows EMIs only as indicative. The designated insurance executive explains cover and add-ons, and the buyer chooses the insurer and cover.
Booking-to-delivery tracker with waiting-period updatesAllotment, paperwork and deliveryThe delivery coordinator confirms allotment and every delivery date before it reaches the buyer. Any change to a promised date, or a request to switch model or color, goes to the sales manager.
Registration, HSRP and RC status trackingAllotment, paperwork and deliveryThe registration executive verifies every document and submits each application on Vahan personally; the automation never submits to a government portal. Name mismatches, other-state addresses and company registrations go to the registration lead.
Ownership transfer and RC document tracker for used vehiclesAllotment, paperwork and deliveryThe documentation executive checks identities and signatures and files every application on Vahan; the automation only tracks and reminds. The used-car manager handles exceptions such as pending challans, lender delays or disputes.
EV subsidy document checks and ownership onboardingAllotment, paperwork and deliveryThe buyer completes Aadhaar authentication and signs the e-voucher on the scheme's own process, and the dealership's subsidy administrator signs, uploads and resolves any mismatch. The service manager approves charging and battery content in line with the OEM's guidance.
Service, PUC and battery check reminders by date and distanceService and repairCustomer relationship executives call lapsed owners and handle every reply that is not a simple booking. The service manager sets reminder windows and frequency limits, and approves EV check content in line with the OEM's guidance.
Online service booking with pick-up and dropService and repairThe service advisor confirms every booking and job description with the owner before work begins. Drivers walk around the vehicle with the owner, and any damage disagreement goes to the works manager.
Job-card status and customer approval for additional workService and repairThe service advisor reviews every estimate and explanation before it is sent, and the owner approves or declines each line. Safety-critical findings such as brakes or battery faults also get a call from the advisor, and estimates above an agreed amount need the works manager's sign-off.
Post-delivery and post-service feedback with service recoveryFeedback, renewals and upgradeThe customer relations manager calls every flagged owner, and the works manager or used-car manager decides on rework, refunds or goodwill. Staff never ask owners to change or inflate OEM survey ratings.
Consented insurance renewal and extended-warranty remindersFeedback, renewals and upgradeThe designated insurance executive explains cover, add-ons and premiums, and the owner chooses. Warranty eligibility and claims are decided under the OEM's terms by the warranty in-charge, not by the automation.
